canonical_policy.name: Behavioral probes become maintained tests
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: If an ad-hoc/manual behavioral probe uniquely demonstrates behavior, preserve that behavior in maintained automated coverage before completion unless equivalent coverage already exists.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Uniquely demonstrated behavior preserved before completion/removal; equivalence must be confirmed, temporary mechanism itself need not remain. Build/compiler/formatter/static checks exempt. Prior records include conversion and removal timing.

Check that changed behavior has useful automated coverage, focusing on behavior rather than line count; look for a regression test on bug fixes where recurrence is plausible; check that behavioral probes were preserved (`verify` step 4). Do not request duplicate tests when equivalent coverage exists.

| Reproduced bug | focused regression test |
| Temporary behavioral probe | convert it to maintained coverage or confirm equivalent coverage exists |

A regression test reproduces the failure before the fix and passes after it. Converting a temporary probe: a curl, PowerShell, or REST check becomes a host integration test; a manual database check becomes a persistence test; reuse existing coverage when it already exercises the behavior, after confirming it really does.

Testing private details; mocking every class; hitting production resources; shared mutable state; assertions that repeat the implementation; assertion-free tests (unless the behavior is "does not throw"); `Task.Delay` to make timing pass; real-provider containers when fidelity is irrelevant; in-memory providers claimed as relational coverage; keeping temporary probes as permanent tests without review.

After API behavior changes: verify controller behavior and integration tests, check response metadata, start the API when startup/composition changed, open the Development Swagger UI, exercise representative endpoints when meaningful, and preserve newly verified behavior as tests (`verify` step 4).

canonical_policy.name: Do not chase coverage percentage
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Do not generate low-value tests merely to increase coverage percentage.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Low-value percentage inflation prohibited; coverage diagnostic only and trivial persistence Add/Get exclusion are explicit separate baseline actions.

canonical_policy.name: HTTP semantics belong to API
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: HTTP status codes and transport response semantics belong to the API layer; Application/Domain must not return IActionResult or ASP.NET Core status codes.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Status values and transport result types prohibited in inner returns; concrete IActionResult/ActionResult/IResult bindings already registered.

context_quotes:
- HTTP status codes and transport response semantics belong to the entry point; the use-case layer and domain model must not return transport result types or HTTP status codes.
- Default: represent common expected outcomes explicitly when useful (`null`, `bool`, a typed outcome), but do not force a generic result-wrapper pattern and do not name use-case outcome categories after HTTP statuses (bad request, unauthorized, forbidden); the entry point maps outcomes such as validation failure, not found, or conflict to HTTP.

- Entry-point mechanism: ASP.NET Core Controllers (decided stack), as controller classes in a `Controllers/` folder of the entry-point project; do not create Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested.
- Transport result types that stay at the entry point: `IActionResult`, `ActionResult<T>`, `IResult`, and status-code constants.
- Remote transport responses that the implementation layer translates: `HttpResponseMessage` and its headers and status.

Raw exception messages to clients; inconsistent anonymous error objects; use-case code depending on HTTP status codes; `Result<T>` everywhere; exceptions for every negative branch; swallowed exceptions; catch/log/rethrow at every layer; duplicate logging; sensitive data in `ProblemDetails`; business rules only in request validators; Minimal API endpoint filters for validation in a Controller project.

canonical_policy.name: Use structured error contracts
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Use ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; keep machine-readable contracts stable and safe.

reviews.boundary_analysis: ProblemDetails/AddProblemDetails and automatic validation binding registered. Generate separate or clearly grouped Swagger documents per supported version (`swagger`), matching runtime routing and metadata. Version changes never override normal HTTP semantics (`http-api`). Test meaningful differences: version routing, version-specific shapes, deprecated versions still operating during support, unsupported-version behavior, shared behavior consistent where intended — without duplicating identical tests per version.

Rules: `.claude/rules/0-core/http-api.md` (response, failure, versioning rules) and the role rule that HTTP semantics belong to the entry point. Keep status behavior consistent across similar endpoints.

- **200 OK** — successful `GET`; `PUT`/`PATCH` returning the updated representation; a `POST` that performs an operation without creating a resource; a query returning data (an empty collection is `200` with `[]`, which is clearer for clients than `204`).
- **201 Created** — the HTTP operation created a new API resource; include `Location` when a stable URI exists. `PUT` may return `201` when it creates the target resource.

  ```csharp
  return CreatedAtAction(nameof(GetById), new { id = created.Id }, created);
  ```

- **202 Accepted** — processing accepted but incomplete (long-running operation, background job, async import, queued work); return an operation id or a `Location` where progress is observable: `AcceptedAtAction(nameof(GetOperation), new { id = operationId }, response)`.
- **204 No Content** — success with no body (`DELETE`, updates where returning the representation adds nothing); a `204` never carries a body. Choose one convention for repeated `DELETE` of an absent resource — `204` (final state holds) or `404` (resource absent) — and apply it consistently across equivalent resources.
- **304 Not Modified** — only for conditional requests (`If-None-Match`/ETag, `If-Modified-Since`) when the cached representation is still valid; never a generic "nothing changed" business response.
- **404 Not Found** — the addressed resource does not exist, or the API deliberately hides it.
- **406 Not Acceptable** — the server cannot produce a representation the client accepts (response negotiation). **415 Unsupported Media Type** — the server does not support the request body format (`Content-Type: application/xml` on a JSON-only endpoint).
- **409 Conflict** — valid request conflicting with current state: duplicate where uniqueness is resource state, incompatible state transition (cancelling a completed order), conflicting concurrent operation, idempotency key reused with a different payload. Not for malformed syntax.
- **412 Precondition Failed** — a supplied precondition is false (`If-Match: "version-7"` while the resource is at `"version-8"`).
- **422 Unprocessable Content** — structurally valid request with invalid semantics or business input (`startDate > endDate`, business rejection that is not a state conflict). Some APIs use `400` for both; follow an established convention. New APIs that distinguish them: `400` = invalid HTTP/request contract, `422` = valid structure, invalid semantics.
- **428 Precondition Required** — the contract requires a precondition the client omitted (missing required `If-Match` → `428`; stale `If-Match` → `412`).
- **429 Too Many Requests** — rate limiting rejected the request; include `Retry-After` when known. Never use it for validation failures.
- **500** — unexpected internal failure without a more specific controlled outcome; centralized handling and `ProblemDetails`.
- **502 Bad Gateway** — this API acts as an intermediary and received an invalid or unusable upstream response; do not map every dependency failure to `502`.
- **503 Service Unavailable** — temporarily unable to serve (maintenance, a critical dependency unavailable for this operation, overload); include `Retry-After` when meaningful.
- **504 Gateway Timeout** — as an intermediary, the upstream did not answer in time. Distinguish client cancellation, our own timeout, and upstream timeout; not every `TaskCanceledException` is a `504`.

| Situation | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Query with representation | `200` |
| Empty collection | `200` + `[]` |
| Resource created | `201` + `Location` when available |
| Accepted, incomplete | `202` |
| Success without body | `204` |
| Conditional cache hit | `304` |
| Malformed/contract-invalid request | `400` |
| Missing/invalid authentication | `401` |
| Authenticated but forbidden | `403` |
| Resource absent | `404` |
| No acceptable response representation | `406` |
| Current-state conflict | `409` |
| Supplied precondition failed | `412` |
| Unsupported request content type | `415` |
| Valid structure, invalid semantics | `422` |
| Required precondition absent | `428` |
| Rate limited | `429` + `Retry-After` when known |
| Unexpected internal failure | `500` |
| Bad upstream response (intermediary) | `502` |
| Temporarily unavailable | `503` |
| Upstream timeout (intermediary) | `504` |
Do not forward every upstream status code to your own API; outbound retry behavior and the inbound response your API returns are separate decisions.

Per-request `HttpClient`; mandating one client model everywhere; retries on unsafe operations without idempotency analysis; unbounded retries; leaking `HttpResponseMessage`; ignored cancellation; dynamic tokens in shared default headers; mapping every upstream failure to one status; resilience pipelines added without understanding their behavior.

- **Hedging** — parallel or delayed duplicate attempts, only for operations safe to run several times (typically idempotent reads against interchangeable endpoints); never writes by default.
- **Inbound rate limiting** — ASP.NET Core rate limiting protects this API and is separate from outbound resilience; rejected requests get `429` with `Retry-After` when useful (`http-api`).

Consider the whole pipeline when listing responses — model binding, validation, authentication/authorization, rate limiting, centralized exception handling, other middleware — not only explicit action branches. Document `201` with `CreatedAtAction`/`CreatedAtRoute` when a canonical URL exists; never `201` for an endpoint returning `200` or `204` for one returning a body. Describe `ProblemDetails`/`ValidationProblemDetails` where useful, without internal exception types, stack traces, SQL, connection strings, or paths in examples.

canonical_policy.name: 401/403 semantics

reviews.boundary_analysis: 401/403 middleware-default ownership, no400 for authentication failure and deliberate consistent404 hiding are prior atomic actions; 403 not fixed by resending same credentials explanatory consequence not new inferred mandate.

Authentication/authorization middleware normally produces `401` (not authenticated or authentication failed) and `403` (authenticated, not permitted) rather than controllers manufacturing them. A deliberate `404` for some forbidden lookups must be a consistent policy (`http-api`).
